title: Piri-Piri Chicken
summary: A spatchcocked whole chicken marinated in a blended chilli, garlic and lemon sauce, then grilled or roasted until charred and juicy.
equipment: barbecue with a lid, or a large roasting tin with a rack

ingredients.item: whole chicken, about 1600 g, spatchcocked (backbone removed and flattened)
ingredients.note: ask the butcher, or use poultry shears

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Blend the piri-piri sauce
steps.text: Blend all the sauce ingredients until smooth. Simmer the sauce in a small pan for 3-4 minutes, which cooks out the raw edge of the garlic and tomato and mellows the chilli's heat slightly, then let it cool.

steps.title: Spatchcock the chicken
steps.text: Cut out the backbone with poultry shears and press down firmly on the breastbone to flatten the bird. Slash the legs and breast 2-3 times so the marinade and heat can reach deeper into the meat.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Coat the chicken with half the sauce, working it both under and over the skin, keeping the other half aside for serving. Cover and refrigerate for 6-24 hours.

steps.title: Barbecue
steps.text: Set up two heat zones on the barbecue, with coals or burners lit on one side only. Place the chicken skin-side up on the cool side, cover with the lid, and cook for 35-45 minutes until the thigh reaches around 70°C, then move it skin-side down over the hot side for 4-6 minutes, watching for flare-ups, until charred and crisp and the breast reaches 74°C and the thigh 77-80°C.

steps.title: Or roast and grill
steps.text: Without a barbecue, heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) for at least 20 minutes, then roast on a rack in a tin, skin-up, for 45-55 minutes until the same temperatures are reached, then finish under the grill (broiler) for 3-4 minutes to char the skin.

steps.title: Char the lemons and rest
steps.text: Grill the lemon halves cut-side down for 3-4 minutes until caramelised. Rest the chicken for 10 minutes, then cut into pieces and serve with the reserved sauce and the grilled lemons.

tips: Simmering the blended sauce briefly before marinating softens the raw chilli bite and deepens the flavour.
Common mistake: using the same sauce for marinating and serving. Keep half back untouched by raw chicken for the table.
Two-zone grilling - cooking through on gentle heat, then charring on fierce heat - gives crisp skin without burning before the meat is cooked.
Reduce the chilli quantity if you want a milder result; the flavour will still come through at half the amount.
Grilling the lemon halves adds a caramelised sweetness that balances the chilli's heat.
storage: Keep cooked chicken in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat until piping hot throughout (74°C); it's also good served cold the next day. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
